title: God, The Forgiving Lord, Is Kind
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: This shabad opens with god, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor. It turns the heart toward nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels envious, unsettled, and small because the shabad keeps comparison inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: Nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God.

lines.translation: God, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor.
He loves His devotees, and He is always merciful to them.
The Patron of the patronless, the Lord of the Universe, the Sustainer of the world,
The Primal Being, the Creator of the Creation.
The Support of the breath of life of His devotees.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਜੋ ਜਪੈ ਸੁ ਹੋਇ ਪੁਨੀਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo jo japai su hoi puneet ||
lines.translation: Whoever meditates on Him is sanctified,
focusing the mind in loving devotional worship.
I am unworthy, lowly and ignorant.
Nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God. ||7||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: god, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor.
The middle movement widens the correction through the Support of the breath of life of His devotees.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God.
